pair_contract.controlled_material_fact: Whether the supplied device evidence establishes a manual, holdable white balance inside the phone's VIDEO recording mode, or establishes that manual white balance exists for stills only and video records with automatic white balance that cannot be locked.
pair_contract.case_1_value: Device evidence (manufacturer support page + photo of the video settings screen) establishes a 'Pro Video' mode with manual white balance in Kelvin that holds the chosen value for the whole clip.
pair_contract.case_2_value: Device evidence (same two sources) states the manual-Kelvin 'Pro' mode is available for photos only; video records with automatic white balance and the app offers no white-balance lock in video.
held_constant_facts: Same vehicle and same verified condition facts: 2016 silver Corolla, repainted rear-right quarter panel that reads lighter than the adjacent door in daylight, 12 cm front bumper scuff, odometer 189,412 km.

Same location and light geometry: open Sharjah used-car lot at 14:40, clear sky, canopy shade line falling across the car near the B-pillar so the front half is in open shade and the rear half in direct sun.
Same immobility constraint: the car cannot be repositioned or re-parked before it leaves, and the neighbouring bays are occupied by cars that cannot be moved.
Same operator: Faisal, a salesperson with no manual-camera experience, shooting handheld, with no tripod, gimbal, reflector, lighting kit or external mic, and speaking on camera while shooting.

Same brief and downstream contract: coverage for a 60-second listing video cut tonight by a separate editor who will not reshoot, requiring spoken walkaround plus wides, mediums, the repainted quarter, the bumper scuff, the odometer, wheels and cabin.
Same time budget: 35 minutes, car leaves for a buyer's inspection at 15:15.

Same remaining device capabilities in both evidence packets: 4K up to 30 fps only, 1080p at 30/60, tap-to-hold focus and exposure in video, auto-HDR on by default and switchable, ~40 GB free storage, and explicit silence on log/flat profiles, other 4K frame rates, 10-bit/ProRes recording and external-mic support.
pair_contract.why: Colour consistency across a shade/sun split is a capture-irreversible risk, and the only three ways to buy it are (a) lock the balance in camera, (b) remove the light variable physically, or (c) restructure coverage and hand the editor a matching handle. The pair holds the physical route closed in both cases — the car cannot be moved and the shade line is fixed — so the correct plan is decided entirely by whether route (a) exists on this handset. In case 1 the professional stance is to set one Kelvin value before the first clip and hold it across every shot, consciously accepting a consistent cast on the secondary zone, and to keep managing brightness separately with tap-to-hold exposure. In case 2 that stance is unavailable and attempting it would be an invented capability; the correct stance shifts to structural control: never let a single take cross the shade line, keep each clip dominated by one light zone with a repeated in-frame reference so the automatic balance lands similarly, pre-roll so it settles, and explicitly escalate the unfixable mismatch to the editor with a deliberate matching reference filmed in both zones. A candidate that answers both cases with the same plan has either invented a video white-balance lock that case 2's evidence denies, or has thrown away a control case 1's evidence grants and paid unnecessary structural cost. Exposure, focus, framing, truth-of-condition and coaching obligations are identical in both and are not the discriminator.

cases.brief: The listing owner has approved the shot intent and you are the camera authority on it: a phone-shot source set the editor will cut into a 60-second used-car listing video tonight. It needs one spoken exterior walkaround by the salesperson plus the complementary coverage the editor will need — wides, mediums, the repainted rear-right quarter panel, the front bumper scuff, the odometer, wheels and cabin. You are not holding the phone. Faisal is. Produce the capture plan and the instructions you will actually give him, in the order you will give them.
cases.context: Open used-car lot in Sharjah, 14:40, clear sky, no haze. The car is a 2016 silver Corolla parked nose-in in a numbered bay. A steel canopy covers the front half of the bay: the shade line falls across the car at roughly the B-pillar, so the bonnet, windscreen and front doors sit in open shade while the rear doors, rear quarters and boot are in direct sun. Condition facts already verified and approved by the listing owner: the rear-right quarter panel was repainted after a parking impact and the new paint reads slightly lighter than the adjacent door in daylight; there is a 12 cm scuff on the front bumper; the odometer reads 189,412 km. Operator: Faisal, a salesperson at the lot. He has filmed cars on his phone before and has never used any manual camera control. He shoots handheld and will be speaking to camera during the walkaround. Device evidence: the manager sent you the manufacturer's support page for the lot's shared phone (a 2024 mid-range Android handset) together with a photo of the phone's video settings screen. Together these two sources establish: video records at up to 3840x2160 at 30 fps, and 1920x1080 at 30 or 60 fps; there is a 'Pro Video' mode that exposes manual white balance in Kelvin and holds the value you set for the duration of the clip; tapping the subject in the video viewfinder sets and holds focus and exposure until you tap away; auto-HDR is on by default and can be switched off in the same menu; about 40 GB of storage is free. The evidence is silent on, and therefore does not establish, any of the following: a log or flat colour profile, any 4K frame rate other than 30, 10-bit or ProRes-style recording, and external-microphone support.
cases.constraints: The buyer's inspection takes the car off the lot at 15:15, 35 minutes from now, and it does not come back tonight. The car cannot be repositioned: the bay is too tight to reverse out and re-park in the time available, and the bays either side hold sold cars that cannot be moved. No tripod, gimbal, reflector, lighting kit or external microphone is on site, and nothing can be sourced before 15:15. Faisal must be able to follow your instructions while talking on camera. The editor is a different person, receives the files tonight and cannot ask for anything to be reshot.
cases.competent_generic_baseline: Tell Faisal to switch to Pro Video, set the white balance manually rather than leaving it automatic, turn on 4K, tap the car to lock focus and exposure before each shot, walk slowly and smoothly around the vehicle at chest height while describing the car, then capture close-ups of the repainted quarter, the bumper scuff, the odometer, the wheels and the cabin, and play a couple of clips back before the car leaves to make sure nothing is blurry or too dark.
professional_criteria: Uses the one control the supplied evidence actually grants as the answer to the shade-line problem: a single Kelvin white balance set in Pro Video before the first clip and kept at that same value for every clip in the set — walkaround, details, odometer and cabin — so the shots cut together without a per-clip colour jump, instead of letting each clip re-balance itself.

Chooses that locked value deliberately against the stated split rather than arbitrarily, and names the accepted cost out loud: whichever zone is not matched will read warm or cool, but as one consistent, gradeable offset the editor can handle, which is a better trade than random drift between adjacent shots.

Keeps brightness as a separate problem from colour: recognizes that the sunlit rear panels and the shaded front half will not both sit inside one phone exposure, and solves it per shot with tap-to-hold exposure on the decision-relevant subject plus position and angle choices — staying inside one light zone per shot, and approaching the sunlit silver panels from an angle that moves the specular hotspot off the surface being shown — rather than one averaged exposure carried through the whole walkaround.

Protects the two proof items under the stated light: the repainted rear-right quarter is shot in its actual sunlit condition at a distance and angle that let the tone difference against the adjacent door remain visible rather than being washed out by glare or quietly avoided, and the odometer is shot with exposure held on the instrument cluster so 189,412 is legible despite the bright exterior behind the operator.

Gives Faisal physically executable cues he can follow while speaking: where to start, distance from the body, phone height relative to the car, walking path around a vehicle that cannot be repositioned, pace, where to stop and hold, when to start and stop recording, and what specifically to do as he reaches the shade line — plus a named coverage list that hands the editor complementary wides, mediums and details instead of one long continuous take.

Fits an on-location QC step inside the 35 minutes and makes it concrete: play back one shade-zone clip and one sun-zone clip full-screen with audio before 15:15, state the specific defect to look for in each, and reshoot by impact rather than in order; then record the locked white-balance value and any remaining known defect in what goes to the editor tonight.

p0_guardrail.trigger: The plan instructs Faisal to use a capture capability the supplied evidence does not establish — for example 4K at 60 or 50 fps, a 24 fps cinematic mode, a log or flat colour profile, 10-bit or ProRes-style recording, or an external microphone — and builds the exposure, motion or audio plan on that assumed capability.

cases.competent_generic_baseline: Since white balance can't be set for video on this phone, leave it on automatic and don't fight it: shoot 4K30, tap the car to hold focus and exposure before each shot, keep the walkaround slow and steady at chest height while Faisal describes the car, then get the repainted quarter, the bumper scuff, the odometer, the wheels and the cabin, check a few clips for blur or darkness before 15:15, and tell the editor the colour may need matching between shots in the grade.
professional_criteria: Reads the evidence precisely and does not import the stills Pro mode into video: because video white balance is automatic with no lock on this handset, colour consistency across the shade/sun split cannot be bought with a setting at all, and the plan says so explicitly rather than hedging around it.

Given that the car also cannot be moved, buys the consistency structurally instead: keeps every cuttable shot dominated by a single light zone, and rules out any pan, walk or reframe that carries the frame across the shade line during a take, because that is precisely where the automatic balance will visibly shift inside one clip — which means restructuring the walkaround into separate shade-side and sun-side pieces rather than one continuous circuit.

Gives the automatic system a consistent thing to react to: repeats roughly the same proportion of silver body panel, sky and ground in frame when starting clips that must cut together, and has Faisal roll a couple of seconds before the useful action so the balance settles before the content the editor will use begins.

Uses the control the evidence does grant — tap to hold focus and exposure — on the sunlit silver panels, the repainted quarter and the odometer through the windscreen, and is explicit with Faisal that this holds brightness and focus but does nothing about the colour shift, so he does not assume the problem is solved.

Escalates the residual capture-irreversible colour mismatch to the editor instead of leaving it to be discovered tonight: identifies which clips were shot in shade and which in sun, and deliberately captures a matching handle — the same panel, or the same neutral surface, filmed briefly in both zones — so the editor has a concrete reference to match against rather than guesswork.

Gives Faisal executable physical instruction and one QC check that fits inside the 35 minutes: distance, phone height, path and pace around a car that cannot be repositioned, where to stop and hold for the repainted quarter at an angle that lets the tone difference stay visible and for the odometer so 189,412 reads, and a back-to-back full-screen playback of one shade clip against one sun clip before 15:15 with a named defect to look for and a single highest-impact reshoot.

p0_guardrail.trigger: The plan instructs Faisal to set, lock or hold a manual or Kelvin white balance while recording video, or to use a log/flat profile, 10-bit/ProRes recording, a 4K frame rate other than 30, or an external microphone — capabilities the supplied evidence either explicitly denies for video or does not establish at all — and builds the colour, exposure or audio plan on that assumed capability.
